claim: 20% of wild type P. aeruginosa PA14 cells reproducibly exhibit c-di-GMP concentrations less than 200 nM during exponential growth
source: Using FRET-based microscopy, we imaged cells from single time points to visualize heterogeneity in c-di-GMP levels. Use of an automated method to segment cells and analyze their fluorescence intensity allowed us to determine that 20% of wild type P. aeruginosa PA14 cells reproducibly exhibit c-di-GMP concentrations less than 200 nM during exponential growth (Figure 1A,B,G).
evidence: Supported by FRET-based microscopy measurements and quantification shown in Figure 1A,B,G

claim: PA5017 is responsible for maintaining the population of cells with reduced c-di-GMP levels
source: However, we identified one gene, PA5017, responsible for maintaining the population of cells with reduced c-di-GMP levels.
evidence: Identified through screening of transposon mutant bank for altered c-di-GMP levels

claim: The protein encoded by PA5017 is a phosphodiesterase
source: Previous characterization has shown that the protein encoded by this gene is a PDE (Roy et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Roy et al., 2012

claim: The PDE activity of PA5017 is required for a c-di-GMP bimodal distribution
source: In-frame deletion of PA5017 (Figure 1C,D,G) and gene complementation experiments (Figure 1E–G), including those using a catalytically inactive mutant, confirmed that the PDE activity of PA5017 is required for a c-di-GMP bimodal distribution.
evidence: Demonstrated through deletion, complementation, and catalytic mutant experiments shown in Figure 1C-G

claim: Pch-mCherry exhibits polar localization in 50% of cells
source: Pch-mCherry exhibited polar localization in 50% of cells (Figure 2A).
evidence: Observed through fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 2A

claim: Polarly localized Pch-mCherry is partitioned to a single cell following cell division
source: Using time-lapse FRET imaging, we observed that polarly localized Pch-mCherry is partitioned to a single cell following cell division (Figure 2B).
evidence: Demonstrated through time-lapse FRET imaging shown in Figure 2B

claim: Pch-mCherry localizes to the pole of the incipient daughter cell that exhibits reduced cellular c-di-GMP following cell division
source: Furthermore, Pch-mCherry localizes to the pole of the incipient daughter cell that exhibits reduced cellular c-di-GMP following cell division (Figure 2B).
evidence: Observed through time-lapse FRET imaging shown in Figure 2B

claim: c-di-GMP heterogeneity occurs mostly through differential polar localization and the subsequent asymmetric partitioning of Pch during cell division
source: These results indicate that c-di-GMP heterogeneity occurs mostly through differential polar localization and the subsequent asymmetric partitioning of Pch during cell division.
evidence: Inferred from the correlation between Pch-mCherry localization and c-di-GMP levels

claim: Localization of Pch-mCherry was abolished in the fliF mutant
source: Localization, or foci formation, of Pch-mCherry was abolished in the fliF mutant (Figure 3A,C)
evidence: Observed through fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 3A,C

claim: More than 99% of ΔfliF cells exhibit c-di-GMP levels greater than 200 nM
source: biosensor activity measurements revealed that more than 99% of ΔfliF cells exhibit c-di-GMP levels greater than 200 nM (Figure 3B).
evidence: Measured using FRET biosensor shown in Figure 3B

claim: An flhF deletion causes Pch-mCherry foci to delocalize from the pole
source: We observed that an flhF deletion also causes Pch-mCherry foci to delocalize from the pole (Figure 3A,C,D).
evidence: Observed through fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 3A,C,D

claim: flhF mutant cells are able to maintain c-di-GMP heterogeneity
source: Nevertheless, biosensor activity showed that flhF mutant cells are able to maintain c-di-GMP heterogeneity (Figure 3B, right panel).
evidence: Measured using FRET biosensor shown in Figure 3B

claim: The flagellum, but not its polar positioning, is required for the maintenance of low c-di-GMP concentrations
source: Thus, the flagellum, but not its polar positioning, is required for the maintenance of low c-di-GMP concentrations.
evidence: Inferred from comparison of fliF and flhF mutant phenotypes

claim: Deletions of cheR, cheY and cheB did not have any effect on Pch-mCherry localization
source: Deletions of the methyl accepting chemoreceptor (MCP) methyltransferase, cheR, and chemotaxis machinery response regulators, cheY and cheB, did not have any effect on Pch-mCherry localization (Figure 4A).
evidence: Observed through fluorescence microscopy quantified in Figure 4A

claim: A cheA null strain lacks Pch-mCherry localization
source: However, we discovered that a cheA null strain lacks Pch-mCherry localization (Figure 4C)
evidence: Observed through fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 4C

claim: A cheA null strain fails to demonstrate c-di-GMP heterogeneity
source: However, we discovered that a cheA null strain lacks Pch-mCherry localization (Figure 4C) and also fails to demonstrate c-di-GMP heterogeneity (Figure 4B,D).
evidence: Measured using FRET biosensor shown in Figure 4B,D

claim: The chemotaxis machinery histidine kinase, CheA, is required for both polar localization and activity of Pch
source: Taken together, these results indicate that the chemotaxis machinery histidine kinase, CheA, is required for both polar localization and activity of Pch.
evidence: Inferred from the effects of cheA deletion on Pch localization and c-di-GMP levels

claim: The CheAH49N phosphotransfer mutant had no effect on Pch-mCherry localization
source: We found that this phosphotransfer mutant conferred by the CheAH49N allele had no effect on Pch-mCherry localization (Figure 4A).
evidence: Observed through fluorescence microscopy quantified in Figure 4A

claim: More than 90% of CheAH49N cells exhibited greater than 200 nM intracellular c-di-GMP, decreasing heterogeneity
source: However, c-di-GMP levels increased relative to wild type, as more than 90% of cells exhibited greater than 200 nM intracellular c-di-GMP, decreasing heterogeneity (Figure 4B).
evidence: Measured using FRET biosensor shown in Figure 4B

claim: The chemotaxis apparatus controls c-di-GMP heterogeneity in a manner dependent on the phosphorylation of CheA
source: The requirement of CheA histidine-49 for the maintenance of low c-di-GMP indicates that the chemotaxis apparatus controls c-di-GMP heterogeneity in a manner dependent on the phosphorylation of CheA.
evidence: Inferred from the effect of CheAH49N mutation on c-di-GMP levels

claim: 93 ± 1% of cells containing both CheA and Pch fusions had these proteins co-localized to the same pole
source: The majority (93 ± 1%) of cells containing both CheA and Pch fusions had these proteins co-localized to the same pole (Figure 5A,B).
evidence: Observed through dual fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 5A,B

claim: The flhF deletion caused Pch-Yfp and CheA-mTq to delocalize from the pole but to still associate
source: Furthermore, the flhF deletion caused Pch-Yfp and CheA-mTq to delocalize from the pole but to still associate (Figure 5A–D).
evidence: Observed through dual fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 5A-D

claim: A functional CheA-mTq fusion localized to the same pole as a functional FliM-mKate2 fusion in 87 ± 3% of cells
source: A functional CheA-mTq fusion localized to the same pole as a functional FliM-mKate2 fusion in 87 ± 3% of cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: Observed through dual fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A–C

claim: CheA and FliM protein complexes were separated by a measurable distance with a median distance of 0.190 ± 0.010 μm
source: However, these two protein complexes were separated by a measurable distance as indicated by a peak in the histogram (median distance of 0.190 ± 0.010 μm) in contrast to the undetectable spacing between Pch-Yfp or Pch-mCherry and CheA-mTq (Figure 5B, Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: Quantified from dual fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 5B and Figure 5—figure supplement 2

claim: Pch is associated with the chemotaxis machinery but not with the flagellar apparatus present at the same pole
source: These co-localization studies indicate Pch is associated with the chemotaxis machinery but not with the flagellar apparatus present at the same pole.
evidence: Inferred from the spatial separation between CheA and FliM versus the co-localization of Pch and CheA

claim: A cheA deletion does not affect FliM-mKate2 polar localization
source: As previous observations have shown that a cheA mutant is still motile (Ferrandez et al., 2002), and a cheA deletion does not affect FliM-mKate2 polar localization (Figure 5—figure supplement 3), these observations indicate that a cheA deletion does not affect flagellar assembly
evidence: Observed through fluorescence microscopy shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 3

claim: A cheA mutant is still motile
source: As previous observations have shown that a cheA mutant is still motile (Ferrandez et al., 2002)
evidence: Supported by citation to Ferrandez et al., 2002

claim: A cheA deletion does not affect flagellar assembly
source: these observations indicate that a cheA deletion does not affect flagellar assembly
evidence: Inferred from FliM localization and motility data

claim: Pch activation and localization is mostly dependent on CheA
source: these observations indicate that a cheA deletion does not affect flagellar assembly and that that Pch activation and localization is mostly dependent on CheA.
evidence: Inferred from the effects of cheA deletion on Pch localization and activity

claim: CheA-mTq specifically precipitates with Pch-VSV-G
source: We found CheA-mTq specifically precipitates with Pch-VSV-G (Figure 5E).
evidence: Demonstrated through co-immunoprecipitation shown in Figure 5E

claim: Pch binds to the chemotaxis machinery protein CheA or to another adaptor protein in complex with CheA
source: Taken together, these results support the conclusion that Pch binds to the chemotaxis machinery protein CheA or to another adaptor protein in complex with CheA.
evidence: Inferred from co-localization and co-immunoprecipitation data

claim: A P. aeruginosa pch mutant reduces swimming and swarming motility as determined by bulk, agar-based assays
source: A P. aeruginosa pch mutant reduces swimming and swarming motility as determined by bulk, agar-based assays (Li et al., 2007; Roy et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Li et al., 2007 and Roy et al., 2012

claim: The majority of Δpch cells were either amotile or traveled at a much lower velocity than wild type
source: We quantified mean cell velocity and determined that the majority of Δpch cells were either amotile or traveled at a much lower velocity than wild type (Figure 6A).
evidence: Quantified from single cell tracking shown in Figure 6A

claim: Ectopically reducing c-di-GMP to levels lower than wild type increased the population of cells with mean velocities between four and eight microns/s and decreased the population of amotile cells
source: Conversely, ectopically reducing c-di-GMP to levels lower than wild type, utilizing a PDE expressing strain, increased the population of cells with mean velocities between four and eight microns/s and decreased the population of amotile cells.
evidence: Observed from single cell tracking data

claim: c-di-GMP levels in wild-type cells have a physiological role in modulating cell velocity
source: These results indicate that the c-di-GMP levels in wild-type cells have a physiological role in modulating cell velocity, as both reducing and increasing c-di-GMP levels affects velocity.
evidence: Inferred from the effects of altering c-di-GMP levels on cell velocity

claim: Approximately 25% of the wild-type cells exhibited at least one reversal in direction for trajectories of 25 microns
source: Approximately 25% of the wild-type cells exhibited at least one reversal in direction for trajectories of 25 microns (Figure 6B).
evidence: Quantified from single cell tracking shown in Figure 6B

claim: At least 60% of cells ectopically expressing a PDE exhibited one or more reversals
source: Reversals were increased in cells ectopically expressing a PDE as at least 60% of cells exhibited one or more reversals.
evidence: Quantified from single cell tracking data

claim: The small percentage of motile Δpch cells exhibited fewer reversals than wild type
source: In contrast, the small percentage of motile Δpch cells exhibited fewer reversals than wild type.
evidence: Quantified from single cell tracking data

claim: More than 95% of ΔcheY cells exhibited no reversals
source: Control strains, ΔcheY and ΔcheB gave the expected results in which more than 95% of ΔcheY cells exhibited no reversals
evidence: Quantified from single cell tracking data

claim: More ΔcheB cells relative to wild type exhibited increased reversals
source: Control strains, ΔcheY and ΔcheB gave the expected results in which more than 95% of ΔcheY cells exhibited no reversals and more ΔcheB cells relative to wild type exhibited increased reversals.
evidence: Quantified from single cell tracking data

claim: c-di-GMP levels act to create heterogeneity not only in cell velocities but also in modulating chemotaxis machinery output
source: These data indicate that c-di-GMP levels act to create heterogeneity not only in cell velocities but also in modulating chemotaxis machinery output.
evidence: Inferred from the effects of c-di-GMP on both velocity and reversal rates

claim: PA3353 did not have a significant effect on either velocity or reversal rate
source: We deleted the homolog of this gene in P. aeruginosa, PA3353, and found this gene did not have a significant effect on either velocity or reversal rate, as both were similar to that of wild type.
evidence: Observed from single cell tracking data

claim: The PilZ domain protein PA3353 does not mediate reduction of cell velocity or inhibition of flagellar motor reversals by c-di-GMP in the conditions used for the assay
source: This result suggests, in the conditions used for the assay, that this PilZ domain protein does not mediate reduction of cell velocity or inhibition of flagellar motor reversals by c-di-GMP.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of effect of PA3353 deletion on velocity and reversals

claim: Individual cell heterogeneity is commonly observed within populations
source: Individual cell heterogeneity is commonly observed within populations, although its molecular basis is largely unknown.
evidence: General scientific knowledge about cellular heterogeneity

claim: c-di-GMP heterogeneity in Pseudomonas aeruginosa is promoted by a specific phosphodiesterase partitioned after cell division
source: In this study, we show that c-di-GMP heterogeneity in Pseudomonas aeruginosa is promoted by a specific phosphodiesterase partitioned after cell division.
evidence: Summary of findings from the study

claim: Subcellular localization and reduction of c-di-GMP levels by this phosphodiesterase is dependent on the histidine kinase component of the chemotaxis machinery, CheA, and its phosphorylation state
source: We found that subcellular localization and reduction of c-di-GMP levels by this phosphodiesterase is dependent on the histidine kinase component of the chemotaxis machinery, CheA, and its phosphorylation state.
evidence: Summary of findings from the study

claim: Individual cell heterogeneity in c-di-GMP concentrations is regulated by the activity and the asymmetrical inheritance of the chemotaxis organelle after cell division
source: Therefore, individual cell heterogeneity in c-di-GMP concentrations is regulated by the activity and the asymmetrical inheritance of the chemotaxis organelle after cell division.
evidence: Summary conclusion from the study findings

claim: c-di-GMP heterogeneity results in a diversity of motility behaviors
source: c-di-GMP heterogeneity results in a diversity of motility behaviors.
evidence: Summary of findings from motility experiments

claim: The generation of diverse intracellular concentrations of c-di-GMP by asymmetric partitioning is likely important to the success and survival of bacterial populations within the environment by allowing a variety of motility behaviors
source: The generation of diverse intracellular concentrations of c-di-GMP by asymmetric partitioning is likely important to the success and survival of bacterial populations within the environment by allowing a variety of motility behaviors.
evidence: Speculative interpretation of the biological significance of the findings

claim: Single cells in an isogenic population display heterogeneity in a variety of physiological parameters including growth rate, chemotaxis, metabolism, nutritional acquisition, and tolerance to noxious stimuli including antibiotics
source: Single cells in an isogenic population display heterogeneity in a variety of physiological parameters including growth rate, chemotaxis, metabolism, nutritional acquisition, and tolerance to noxious stimuli including antibiotics (Balaban et al., 2004; Shibata and Ueda, 2008; Lidstrom and Konopka, 2010; Wakamoto et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations

claim: Second messenger-based signaling can be a mechanism by which environmental signals are rapidly translated into phenotypic heterogeneity
source: Second messenger-based signaling, having a global impact on cellular physiology (Romling et al., 2013), can be a mechanism by which environmental signals are rapidly translated into phenotypic heterogeneity.
evidence: Supported by citation and general knowledge

claim: The bacterial second messenger c-di-GMP is synthesized and degraded by diguanylate cyclases (DGCs) and phosphodiesterases (PDEs) to regulate diverse processes including cell-cycle progression, motility, and exopolysaccharide production
source: The bacterial second messenger c-di-GMP is synthesized and degraded by diguanylate cyclases (DGCs) and phosphodiesterases (PDEs) to regulate diverse processes including cell-cycle progression, motility, and exopolysaccharide production (Romling et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Romling et al., 2013

claim: FRET microscopy analysis using a c-di-GMP biosensor revealed that the concentration of the second messenger c-di-GMP varies bimodally in populations of diverse bacterial species
source: FRET microscopy analysis using this biosensor revealed that the concentration of the second messenger c-di-GMP varies bimodally in populations of diverse bacterial species (Christen et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Christen et al., 2010

claim: Caulobacter crescentus exhibits an asymmetric cell cycle in that the two daughter cells have unique morphologies and functions
source: One species we examined, Caulobacter crescentus, in contrast to other well-studied gram-negative bacteria, exhibits an asymmetric cell cycle in that the two daughter cells have unique morphologies and functions.
evidence: Established knowledge about C. crescentus

claim: Only the daughter swarmer cell with a polar flagellum is motile in C. crescentus, and only the stalk cell, with the exopolysaccharide containing holdfast, can undergo cell division
source: Only the daughter swarmer cell with a polar flagellum is motile, and only the stalk cell, with the exopolysaccharide containing holdfast, can undergo cell division (Tsokos and Laub, 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Tsokos and Laub, 2012

claim: A c-di-GMP synthesizing enzyme, PleD, is localized and activated in the stalked cell of C. crescentus
source: It has been known that a c-di-GMP synthesizing enzyme, PleD, is localized and activated in the stalked cell (Paul et al., 2004; Aldridge et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citations to Paul et al., 2004 and Aldridge et al., 2003

claim: The daughter cell that does not inherit the flagellum following cell division rapidly synthesizes a new flagellum in P. aeruginosa
source: The daughter cell that does not inherit the flagellum following cell division rapidly synthesizes a new flagellum (Suzuki and Iino, 1980).
evidence: Supported by citation to Suzuki and Iino, 1980

claim: The daughter cell with the lower c-di-GMP concentration after cell division was previously demonstrated to inherit the single polar flagellum
source: The daughter cell with the lower c-di-GMP concentration after cell division was previously demonstrated to inherit the single polar flagellum, suggesting this asymmetry is not a stochastic process (Christen et al., 2010).
evidence: Supported by citation to Christen et al., 2010

claim: An intact flagellar basal body rod-hook structure is required for expression of the chemotaxis machinery
source: However, an intact flagellar basal body rod-hook structure is additionally required for expression of the chemotaxis machinery (Dasgupta et al., 2003), which is also polarly localized in P. aeruginosa (Guvener et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to Dasgupta et al., 2003 and Guvener et al., 2006

claim: The chemotaxis machinery is polarly localized in P. aeruginosa
source: However, an intact flagellar basal body rod-hook structure is additionally required for expression of the chemotaxis machinery (Dasgupta et al., 2003), which is also polarly localized in P. aeruginosa (Guvener et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Guvener et al., 2006

claim: The chemotaxis machinery is a signal transduction system that facilitates directed navigation in the presence of chemical gradients and random navigation in uniform environments
source: The chemotaxis machinery is a signal transduction system that facilitates directed navigation in the presence of chemical gradients and random navigation in uniform environments (Wadhams and Armitage, 2004; Sourjik and Wingreen, 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Wadhams and Armitage, 2004 and Sourjik and Wingreen, 2012

claim: Counter clockwise rotation of the flagellum propels the cell forward in a smooth, straight trajectory, and clockwise rotation causes the cell to tumble and reorient in many bacterial species
source: For many species of bacteria, counter clockwise rotation of the flagellum propels the cell forward in a smooth, straight trajectory, and clockwise rotation causes the cell to tumble and reorient (Berg and Brown, 1972)
evidence: Supported by citation to Berg and Brown, 1972

claim: In cells with a unipolar flagellum, clockwise rotation causes the cell to reverse and then reorient
source: or, in the case of the cell with a unipolar flagellum, to reverse and then reorient (Wadhams and Armitage, 2004; Xie et al., 2011; Qian et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Wadhams and Armitage, 2004; Xie et al., 2011; Qian et al., 2013

claim: Clockwise rotation is initiated by phosphorylated CheY binding to the flagellar rotor
source: Clockwise rotation is initiated by phosphorylated CheY binding to the flagellar rotor (Baker et al., 2006)
evidence: Supported by citation to Baker et al., 2006

claim: MCPs control the rate of CheY phosphorylation by CheA
source: and MCPs control the rate of CheY phosphorylation by CheA (Vladimirov and Sourjik, 2009; Hazelbauer and Lai, 2010).
evidence: Supported by citations to Vladimirov and Sourjik, 2009 and Hazelbauer and Lai, 2010

claim: Constitutively active CheR methylates MCPs, whereas phosphorylated CheB demethylates MCPs
source: Constitutively active CheR methylates MCPs, of which P. aeruginosa possesses 26, whereas phosphorylated CheB demethylates MCPs (Baker et al., 2006).
evidence: Supported by citation to Baker et al., 2006

claim: P. aeruginosa possesses 26 MCPs
source: Constitutively active CheR methylates MCPs, of which P. aeruginosa possesses 26, whereas phosphorylated CheB demethylates MCPs (Baker et al., 2006).
evidence: Stated as fact in the text

claim: Methylation specifically decreases MCP affinity for its ligand and increases CheA kinase activity
source: Methylation specifically decreases MCP affinity for its ligand (Sourjik and Berg, 2002) and increases CheA kinase activity.
evidence: Supported by citation to Sourjik and Berg, 2002

claim: c-di-GMP binds the YcgR protein and this complex interacts with the flagellar motor to reduce velocity and inhibit rotor reversal events in E. coli and S. Typhimurium
source: It is known in E. coli and S. Typhimurium that c-di-GMP binds the YcgR protein and this complex interacts with the flagellar motor to reduce velocity and inhibit rotor reversal events (Ryjenkov et al., 2006; Boehm et al., 2010; Paul et al., 2010; Zorraquino et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to Ryjenkov et al., 2006; Boehm et al., 2010; Paul et al., 2010; Zorraquino et al., 2013

claim: Pch has been shown to be activated by cAMP
source: Interestingly, the Pch PDE has been shown to be activated by another molecule controlled by external signals, cAMP (Roy et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to Roy et al., 2012

claim: Populations of motile E. coli cells exhibit a variety of chemotaxis responses to chemical gradients
source: Populations of motile E. coli cells have been noted to exhibit a variety of chemotaxis responses to chemical gradients (Koshland, 1980; Spudich and Koshland, 1976).
evidence: Supported by citations to Koshland, 1980 and Spudich and Koshland, 1976

claim: Populations with diversity in chemotaxis behavior may have an advantage when encountering a variety of chemical gradients
source: These authors and others have speculated that populations with diversity in such behavior may have an advantage when encountering a variety of chemical gradients (Vladimirov and Sourjik, 2009; Sourjik and Wingreen, 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to Vladimirov and Sourjik, 2009 and Sourjik and Wingreen, 2012

claim: The diversity in c-di-GMP levels in P. aeruginosa likely generates variation in the chemotactic response to a variety of chemical gradients and may be a strategy to maximize survival in unpredictable environments
source: Although our observations were performed in a uniform environment, it is likely that the diversity in c-di-GMP levels in P. aeruginosa also generates variation in the chemotactic response to a variety of chemical gradients and may therefore be a strategy to maximize survival in unpredictable environments.
evidence: Speculative interpretation of the biological significance

claim: Population differences in c-di-GMP are not simply stochastic but involve a specific molecular mechanism associated with the variation in cellular inheritance of specific organelles
source: This work indicates that population differences in the second messenger, c-di-GMP, are not simply stochastic but involve a specific molecular mechanism associated with the variation in cellular inheritance of specific organelles.
evidence: Summary conclusion from the study findings

claim: Similar mechanisms for generating heterogeneity may be associated with other organelles such as pili, paralogous chemotaxis clusters, or flagella
source: In this regard, it is interesting to speculate that similar mechanisms for generating heterogeneity may be associated with other organelles such as pili, paralogous chemotaxis clusters, or flagella, which are inherited in an uneven fashion even in organisms with multiple flagellar organelles such as E. coli (Ping, 2010).
evidence: Speculative extension of findings to other systems

claim: Organelle-based partitioning of cellular proteins could be a broader mechanism by which bacteria generate cellular diversity within populations after cell division
source: Organelle-based partitioning of cellular proteins could therefore be a broader mechanism by which bacteria generate cellular diversity within populations after cell division.
evidence: Speculative generalization of the mechanism

claim: It is likely that complex formation between Pch and CheA occurs via an adaptor protein
source: It is likely that complex formation between Pch and CheA occurs via an adaptor protein.
evidence: Inferred from the lack of known direct interaction domains

claim: Pch lacks CheW-like and response regulator receiver domains
source: Pch lacks such domains, and as receiver domains are typically phosphorylated by histidine kinases, it is unlikely Pch is phosphorylated by CheA.
evidence: Inferred from domain analysis

claim: It is unlikely Pch is phosphorylated by CheA
source: Pch lacks such domains, and as receiver domains are typically phosphorylated by histidine kinases, it is unlikely Pch is phosphorylated by CheA.
evidence: Inferred from lack of receiver domains

claim: Pch possesses GAF, PAS, and PAC sensory input domains and a degenerate GGDEF domain in addition to an EAL domain
source: Pch possesses, in addition to an EAL domain that confers PDE activity, GAF, PAS, and PAC sensory input domains and a degenerate GGDEF domain.
evidence: Domain analysis of Pch protein

claim: GGDEF domains have been shown to interact with receiver-like adaptor domains
source: GGDEF domains confer DGC activity when functional, and have been shown to interact with receiver-like adaptor domains (Chan et al., 2004).
evidence: Supported by citation to Chan et al., 2004

claim: An unidentified receiver domain protein could serve as an adaptor mediating an association between the Pch GGDEF domain and CheA
source: This interaction suggests that an unidentified receiver domain protein could serve as an adaptor mediating an association between the Pch GGDEF domain and CheA.
evidence: Speculative model based on known domain interactions

claim: Pch-mCherry localization appears to be more diffuse in the cheA deletion than in the fliF deletion
source: Evidence for additional interactions includes the observations that Pch-mCherry localization appears to be more diffuse in the cheA deletion than in the fliF deletion.
evidence: Observed from fluorescence microscopy

claim: FliF is required for assembly of a flagellar basal-body rod-hook structure that facilitates secretion of the FliA anti-sigma factor, FlgM
source: FliF is required for assembly of a flagellar basal-body rod-hook structure that facilitates secretion of the FliA anti-sigma factor, FlgM (Karlinsey et al., 2000).
evidence: Supported by citation to Karlinsey et al., 2000

claim: FlgM secretion enables FliA mediated expression of the P. aeruginosa flagellar regulon Class IV genes
source: FlgM secretion enables FliA mediated expression of the P. aeruginosa flagellar regulon Class IV genes (Dasgupta et al., 2003).
evidence: Supported by citation to Dasgupta et al., 2003

claim: A minority of cells exhibited high c-di-GMP concentrations, yet showed polarly localized Pch
source: Interestingly, the Pch PDE has been shown to be activated by another molecule controlled by external signals, cAMP (Roy et al., 2012). We observed that a minority of cells exhibited high c-di-GMP concentrations, yet showed polarly localized Pch (Figure 2B).
evidence: Observed from FRET microscopy shown in Figure 2B

claim: In cells with high c-di-GMP but polarly localized Pch, Pch could be lacking a specific form of allosteric activation
source: In these cells, Pch could be lacking a specific form of allosteric activation.
evidence: Speculative explanation for observed data

claim: The requirement for the chemotaxis machinery to stimulate c-di-GMP turnover ensures that heterogeneity in c-di-GMP levels occurs preferentially in motile and chemotactic competent populations
source: The requirement for the chemotaxis machinery to stimulate c-di-GMP turnover ensures that heterogeneity in c-di-GMP levels occurs preferentially in motile and chemotactic competent populations.
evidence: Inferred from the dependence of Pch activity on chemotaxis machinery

claim: Heterogeneity in c-di-GMP levels within a population confers diversity in cell reversal rates and in cell velocities
source: Therefore, heterogeneity in c-di-GMP levels within a population confers diversity in cell reversal rates and in cell velocities.
evidence: Inferred from the effects of c-di-GMP on motility parameters
